features.principle: a limited palette with one committed accent and a light ground
features.productAssumption: none — colour carries no information architecture
features.harm: none beyond contrast, which the token gate enforces
features.rationale: colour is a visual principle, not a structural claim about the product.

features.principle: a spacing rhythm and information density
features.productAssumption: none — density is a reading comfort, not an IA
features.benefit: comfortable scanning at the reference's tempo
features.harm: a dense rhythm can crowd a small dataset, a loose one can inflate scroll
features.rationale: density is a principle that survives a change of subject matter.

features.productAssumption: that the product has imagery to show
features.benefit: none — the benefit depends entirely on having images
features.harm: the renderer substitutes decorative initials for absent photography, inflating the page and implying a catalogue the product is not
features.rationale: the product has no media field and never asks for photographs, so a media-led balance has nothing to lead with. The reference's media aspect is rejected while its palette and density still transfer.

features.principle: more than one record per row on a wide viewport
features.productAssumption: that the task is comparison or browsing
features.harm: a checklist scanned top-to-bottom loses its place when items sit side by side
features.rationale: the task is checking what is present, read in one column; the reference's multi-column rhythm is adapted to a single column and kept only for desktop width.

features.productAssumption: that there is more than one destination
features.harm: a heavy header over a single-destination product spends attention on nothing
features.rationale: the product has one destination, so the header keeps the reference's type but not its prominence.

features.observed: product cards with price placement and a save affordance
features.principle: show price and a save control on each card
features.productAssumption: that the product sells things and users collect them
features.harm: a price slot with no price and a save control with nothing to save
features.rationale: the product has neither prices nor a save requirement, so these affordances would render empty.
